prototype_feel_reasons: The bread asset retains a conspicuous white rectangular source background that does not match the rounded candidate card.
Candidate dishes use inconsistent framing: some appear as clean cutouts, while others retain plates, bowls, or rectangular backgrounds of visibly different sizes.
The faded completed candidates become extremely washed out, making their cards look unfinished rather than intentionally disabled.
Card shadows and pale green lower-edge treatments are uneven and sometimes read as accidental clipping or duplicated layers.
Dish scale and vertical positioning vary substantially across the 3x3 grid, weakening alignment and visual rhythm.
The tray composition is polished, but the candidate grid below feels provisionally assembled by comparison.
issues: candidate grid / bread card — raw white rectangular image boundary is plainly visible against the rounded off-white card — remove the source background or mask the image within the card using matching border-radius and overflow:hidden

candidate grid / completed rice, fried chicken, potato salad, and soup cards — opacity reduction washes out both subject and container until edges and shadows become indistinct — keep the card structure opaque and apply a controlled desaturation/overlay treatment to the dish only

candidate grid / card framing — dish assets have inconsistent apparent scale, padding, and baseline alignment — define a shared image viewport and normalize object-fit:contain sizing and object-position
candidate grid / card bottoms — pale green shadow or accent layers appear clipped and inconsistent between cells — standardize the card radius, overflow behavior, and shadow/accent geometry

candidate grid / dish backgrounds — mixed transparent cutouts, visible plates, and the bread's rectangular field create inconsistent presentation — export all candidates with transparent backgrounds or intentionally frame every candidate using the same plate/card treatment
overall mobile composition — large vertical gaps around the status marks and grid make the lower section feel loosely assembled — tighten and regularize spacing with a consistent vertical rhythm
